weeks.title: Why businesses need statistics
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki business me data se decisions kaise lete hain: descriptive vs inferential statistics, population vs sample, aur mean, median, weighted average jaise simple summaries ka sahi use.
concepts: **Business statistics** data ko collect, organise, summarise aur interpret karne ka tareeka hai taaki manager guess ki jagah evidence se decision le. Jaise ek kirana chain dekhti hai ki kaunsa item kis din zyada bikta hai, ya ek bank dekhta hai ki kaunse customers loan default karte hain.

**Descriptive statistics** jo data haath me hai usse summarise karti hai (average sales, top-selling category, monthly growth). **Inferential statistics** sample se poori population ke baare me conclusion nikalti hai, jaise 500 customers ke survey se saare 2 lakh customers ki satisfaction ka andaaza.

**Population** woh poora group hai jiske baare me jaanna hai (saare customers, saare invoices). **Sample** uska chhota hissa hai jo actually measure kiya. Population ka number **parameter** kehlata hai (μ, p) aur sample ka number **statistic** (x̄, p̂).

**Data ke types by source and time**: primary data aap khud collect karte ho (survey), secondary data pehle se available hota hai (RBI, company reports). **Cross-sectional** data ek time pe kai units ka hota hai (aaj 50 stores ki sales), **time-series** ek unit ka kai time points pe (ek store ki 24 mahino ki sales).

**Mean vs median**: mean saari values ka average hai, par ek bada outlier (jaise festival day sale ya CEO ki salary) usse kheench leta hai. Median beech wali value hai aur outliers se kam affect hoti hai, isliye skewed business data (income, house prices, order value) me median zyada 'typical' value batata hai.

**Weighted mean** tab use hota hai jab har value ka importance alag ho: average price per kg = total revenue / total quantity, na ki prices ka simple average. Grouped data (class intervals) me har class ka midpoint lekar frequency se weight karte hain.
**Percentage change** = (new − old) / old × 100. Yaad rakho ki 20% girne ke baad 20% badhne se wapas start pe nahi aate, kyunki dono percentages alag base pe lagte hain.

**Charts**: categories ke liye bar chart ya pie chart, numerical data ki distribution ke liye histogram, aur time ke saath trend ke liye line chart. Galat chart (jaise 15 categories ka pie) message ko confuse kar deta hai.

example.problem: Ek kirana store ki ek hafte ki daily sales (₹ hazaar me): 12, 15, 11, 18, 40, 14, 16. Saturday ko festival ki wajah se 40 aaya. Mean aur median nikalo aur batao ki 'normal din' ki sales ke liye kaunsa better hai.
steps: Sort karo: 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 40. n = 7 odd hai, toh median 4th value hai = 15.
Dekho: 7 me se 6 din ki sales 18 se kam ya barabar hai. Mean ko 40 wala festival day upar kheench raha hai.
**Answer**: mean = ₹18 hazaar, median = ₹15 hazaar; normal din ke liye median (₹15 hazaar) better summary hai.

mistakes: Weighted situation me simple average lena. Alag quantities pe alag prices ho toh average price = total revenue / total quantity, prices ka seedha average nahi.
Successive percentage changes ko jodna. −20% aur +20% ka net 0% nahi hota; multiply karo: 0.8 × 1.2 = 0.96, yaani net −4%.
Sample statistic ko population parameter samajh lena. Survey ka 64% sirf sample ka number hai; population ke baare me baat karne ke liye inference chahiye.
revision: Descriptive = jo data hai usse summarise karo; inferential = sample se population ke baare me conclusion.
Parameter population ka number (μ, p), statistic sample ka number (x̄, p̂).
Skewed data me median, symmetric data me mean achha summary hai.
Weighted mean = Σ(w · x) / Σw; grouped data me midpoints use karo.
% change = (new − old) / old × 100; successive changes multiply hote hain.

questions.question: Ek retail company apni annual report me likhti hai: 'Pichhle saal hamare 20 stores ki average monthly sales ₹42 lakh thi.' Yeh statistics ki kaunsi branch ka example hai?
questions.explanation: Company apne saare 20 stores ka actual data summarise kar rahi hai, kisi badi population ke baare me andaaza nahi laga rahi. Isliye yeh descriptive statistics hai. Trap: 'average' shabd dekh ke inferential sochna; inference tab hota jab sample se kisi badi population ka conclusion nikalte.

questions.question: Ek bank ke 2 lakh customers hain. Bank inme se 500 customers ka survey karke app satisfaction naapta hai. Yahan 2 lakh customers kya kehlaayenge?
questions.explanation: Jis poore group ke baare me bank jaanna chahta hai woh population hai, yaani saare 2 lakh customers. 500 surveyed customers sample hain. Parameter aur statistic numbers hote hain (jaise satisfaction %), groups nahi.

questions.question: Ek wholesaler ne ek din me 40 kg rice ₹50/kg pe, 60 kg ₹60/kg pe aur 100 kg ₹45/kg pe becha. Us din ka average selling price per kg kya hai?
questions.explanation: Revenue = 40 × 50 + 60 × 60 + 100 × 45 = 2000 + 3600 + 4500 = 10100. Total quantity = 200 kg. Average = 10100 / 200 = ₹50.50. Trap: teen prices ka simple average (50 + 60 + 45) / 3 = ₹51.67 lena, jo quantities ko ignore karta hai. ₹101 tab aata jab sirf 100 kg se divide karte.

questions.question: Ek product ki sales Q1 me pichhle quarter se 20% giri aur Q2 me Q1 se 20% badhi. Start ke comparison me net change kya hai?
questions.explanation: Agar start 100 hai toh Q1 = 100 × 0.8 = 80, aur Q2 = 80 × 1.2 = 96. Net change = (96 − 100) / 100 = −4%. Trap: −20% + 20% = 0% jodna; doosra 20% chhote base (80) pe lagta hai, isliye pura recover nahi hota.

questions.question: Ek startup ke 5 employees ki monthly salary (₹ hazaar): 20, 22, 25, 28, 205 (aakhri founder ki hai). 'Typical employee' ki salary batane ke liye kaunsa measure aur kitni value sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Mean = 300 / 5 = ₹60 hazaar, jo 5 me se 4 logon se bahut zyada hai kyunki 205 ek outlier hai. Median (beech wali value) = ₹25 hazaar outlier se affect nahi hota. Trap: mean ko hamesha best average maan lena. Is data me koi value repeat nahi hoti, toh mode bhi meaningful nahi hai.

questions.question: Ek D2C brand ke 50 orders ki value (₹) ka frequency table: 0–200: 10 orders, 200–400: 25 orders, 400–600: 10 orders, 600–800: 5 orders. Midpoints use karke average order value estimate karo.
questions.explanation: Midpoints 100, 300, 500, 700. Σ(f × m) = 10 × 100 + 25 × 300 + 10 × 500 + 5 × 700 = 1000 + 7500 + 5000 + 3500 = 17000. Mean = 17000 / 50 = ₹340. Trap: midpoints ka simple average (100 + 300 + 500 + 700) / 4 = ₹400 lena jo frequencies ignore karta hai; ₹300 sirf sabse badi class (modal class) ka midpoint hai.

weeks.title: Measurement scales, centre and spread
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki variable kis scale pe naapa gaya hai (nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio) aur us hisaab se mean, median, mode, range, variance, SD aur coefficient of variation ka sahi choice kaise karte hain.
concepts: **Categorical vs numerical variables**: categorical variable group batata hai (payment mode, city, product category), numerical variable quantity naapta hai. Numerical **discrete** ho sakta hai (ek din me orders ki ginti) ya **continuous** (delivery time, weight).

**Nominal scale**: sirf naam ya label, koi order nahi (UPI / card / cash, PIN code, employee ID). **Ordinal scale**: order hai par gaps equal nahi (rating 1 se 5, grade A/B/C, 'small/medium/large' pack).

**Interval scale**: equal gaps hain par asli zero nahi, isliye ratio meaningful nahi (temperature in °C: 20°C, 10°C se 'double garam' nahi). **Ratio scale**: asli zero hai, ratio meaningful hai (revenue, units sold, age, weight). Zyada tar business numbers ratio scale pe hote hain.

**Kaunsa average kab**: nominal ke liye sirf mode, ordinal ke liye median (aur mode), interval/ratio ke liye mean bhi. Rating 1–5 ka mean log nikaalte hain par strictly yeh ordinal data hai, isliye median safer hai.

**Dispersion kyun zaroori hai**: do suppliers ka average delivery time same ho sakta hai, par jiska spread kam hai woh zyada reliable hai. Inventory planning, quality control aur risk sab spread pe depend karte hain, sirf average pe nahi.

**Range, IQR, variance, SD**: range = max − min (outlier se bahut affect). IQR = Q3 − Q1 (beech ke 50% ka spread, robust). Population variance σ² = Σ(x − μ)² / N, sample variance s² = Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1). SD = √variance, aur iski unit data wali hi hoti hai.
**Coefficient of variation** CV = SD / mean × 100%. Alag scale ya alag mean wale do series ki relative variability compare karne ke liye CV use karo, sirf SD nahi.
**Linear change ka asar**: har value ko a se multiply karke b jodo (y = a·x + b) toh new mean = a·mean + b, new SD = |a| · SD. Fixed amount jodne se spread nahi badalta, sirf centre khisakta hai.

example.problem: Do suppliers ke last 5 deliveries ka time (days): Supplier A: 4, 5, 6, 5, 5. Supplier B: 2, 8, 5, 3, 7. Dono ka mean aur sample SD nikalo. Reliable supplier kaun hai?
steps: A ke deviations: −1, 0, 1, 0, 0. Squares ka sum = 1 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 2.
Sample variance A = 2 / (5 − 1) = 0.5, SD A = √0.5 ≈ 0.71 days.
B ke deviations: −3, 3, 0, −2, 2. Squares ka sum = 9 + 9 + 0 + 4 + 4 = 26.
Sample variance B = 26 / 4 = 6.5, SD B = √6.5 ≈ 2.55 days.
**Answer**: dono ka mean 5 days hai, par SD A ≈ 0.71 aur SD B ≈ 2.55; Supplier A zyada reliable (consistent) hai.

mistakes: Nominal data ka mean nikalna. PIN code ya product code ka average meaningless hai; aise data ke liye mode use karo.
Sample data pe n se divide karna. Sample variance ke liye (n − 1) se divide karo; n tab jab poori population ka data ho.
Alag mean wali series ko sirf SD se compare karna. Mean 200 aur SD 30 wali series, mean 50 aur SD 10 wali se relatively kam variable hai; CV compare karo.
revision: NOIR: Nominal (label), Ordinal (order), Interval (equal gaps, no true zero), Ratio (true zero).
Nominal → mode, ordinal → median, interval/ratio → mean bhi.
s² = Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1); SD = √variance.
CV = SD / mean × 100% se relative spread compare karo.
y = a·x + b ⇒ mean_y = a·mean_x + b, SD_y = |a|·SD_x.

questions.question: Ek food delivery app customers se rating leta hai: 1 = Very poor, 2 = Poor, 3 = Average, 4 = Good, 5 = Excellent. Yeh variable kis scale pe hai?
questions.explanation: Ratings me clear order hai (5, 4 se better hai), par 'Poor' se 'Average' ka gap 'Good' se 'Excellent' ke gap ke barabar hai, yeh guarantee nahi. Isliye yeh ordinal hai. Trap: numbers dekh ke interval ya ratio maan lena; numbers yahan sirf order ke labels hain.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa variable ratio scale pe hai?
questions.explanation: Revenue me asli zero hai (₹0 matlab koi revenue nahi) aur ratio meaningful hai (₹20 lakh, ₹10 lakh ka double hai). PIN code nominal hai, grade ordinal hai, aur °C interval hai kyunki 0°C 'temperature ka absence' nahi hai. Trap: °C ko ratio samajhna kyunki usme bhi numbers aur equal gaps hain.

questions.question: 1,000 customers ka 'preferred payment mode' (UPI, debit card, credit card, cash on delivery) record kiya gaya. Central tendency ke liye kaunsa measure sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Payment mode nominal variable hai: categories ka koi order nahi, toh median ya mean ka matlab nahi banta. Sirf mode (sabse common category) meaningful hai. SD to spread ka measure hai, centre ka nahi.

questions.question: Ek showroom me 5 random din ki footfall: 120, 130, 110, 140, 100. Isko sample maan ke sample standard deviation nikalo.
questions.explanation: Mean = 600 / 5 = 120. Deviations: 0, 10, −10, 20, −20; squares ka sum = 0 + 100 + 100 + 400 + 400 = 1000. Sample variance = 1000 / 4 = 250, SD = √250 ≈ 15.81. Trap: n = 5 se divide karke 200 aur √200 ≈ 14.14 (population formula); 250 aur 200 variances hain, SD nahi.

questions.question: Product A ki daily sales: mean 200 units, SD 30 units. Product B: mean 50 units, SD 10 units. Relatively zyada variable (kam predictable) kaun hai?
options: B, kyunki uska CV 20% hai jo A ke 15% se zyada hai
A, kyunki uska SD zyada hai
questions.explanation: CV A = 30 / 200 = 15%, CV B = 10 / 50 = 20%. Mean ke relative B ka spread zyada hai, isliye B kam predictable hai. Trap: sirf SD (30 > 10) dekh ke A chunna, jabki dono ke means bahut alag hain.

questions.question: Ek company me employees ki monthly salary ka mean ₹30,000 aur SD ₹5,000 hai. Har employee ki salary 10% badhai gayi aur upar se ₹2,000 fixed allowance diya gaya. Naya mean aur SD kya hai?
questions.explanation: New salary = 1.1 × x + 2000. Mean = 1.1 × 30000 + 2000 = ₹35,000. SD = 1.1 × 5000 = ₹5,500; fixed ₹2,000 sabko same milta hai, toh spread nahi badalta. Trap: SD me bhi 2,000 jod dena (₹7,500), ya mean me allowance bhool jaana (₹33,000).

weeks.title: From data to probability for decisions
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki past data ki relative frequencies se probability distribution kaise banti hai, aur us distribution se expected demand, expected profit aur stocking jaise business decisions kaise lete hain.
concepts: **Probability ke teen nazariye**: classical (saare outcomes equally likely, jaise fair dice), **empirical / relative frequency** (past data: 1,000 me se 400 visitors ne cart me daala toh P ≈ 0.4), aur subjective (expert ka judgement, jaise naye product launch ki success). Business me zyada tar empirical probability use hoti hai.

**Sample space aur event**: sample space saare possible outcomes ka set hai, event uska koi subset. Jaise kal ki demand {20, 30, 40, 50} me se kuch bhi ho sakti hai; 'demand kam se kam 40' ek event hai.

**Basic rules**: 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1, saare outcomes ki probability ka sum 1. Complement: P(not A) = 1 − P(A). Addition rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); 'both' wala hissa do baar gina jaata hai, isliye minus.

**Probability distribution** har possible value ke saath uski probability ki list hai. 50 din ke data me demand 20 cakes 10 din aayi toh P(20) = 10 / 50 = 0.2. Isse future ke liye ek model ban jaata hai.
**Cumulative probability** P(X ≤ k) ya P(X ≥ k) se service-level jaise sawaal answer hote hain: 'kitni probability hai ki 40 cakes stock karne pe bhi kam padenge?'
**Expected value** E[X] = Σ x · P(x) long-run average hai. Expected demand ya expected profit decisions ka basic tool hai, par yeh ek din ka guaranteed result nahi, bahut saare dino ka average hai.

**Decision under uncertainty**: har option (jaise 30 ya 40 units stock karna) ke liye har demand scenario ka profit nikalo, phir probabilities se weight karke expected profit compare karo. Sirf 'average demand pe profit' nikalna galat hai kyunki unsold stock aur lost sales ka asar miss ho jaata hai.

example.problem: Ek bakery ne 50 din ka data dekha: demand 20 cakes (10 din), 30 cakes (20 din), 40 cakes (15 din), 50 cakes (5 din). Cake ki cost ₹100, price ₹300, bacha hua cake waste. Bakery ko 30 cakes banane chahiye ya 40?
steps: Probabilities: P(20) = 10/50 = 0.2, P(30) = 0.4, P(40) = 0.3, P(50) = 0.1. Sum = 1, valid distribution.
30 banaye (cost ₹3,000): demand 20 pe revenue 20 × 300 = 6,000, profit 3,000; demand ≥ 30 pe revenue 9,000, profit 6,000.
**Answer**: 40 cakes banana better hai (expected profit ₹5,600 vs ₹5,400), jabki expected demand sirf 33 hai, kyunki margin (₹200) waste cost (₹100) se zyada hai.

mistakes: Addition rule me overlap minus karna bhool jaana. UPI aur card dono use karne wale customers do baar gine jaate hain; P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) lo.
Expected demand pe hi profit nikaal ke use expected profit maan lena. Pehle har scenario ka profit nikalo, phir unka weighted average lo.
Distribution me probabilities ka sum check na karna. Agar sum 1 nahi hai ya koi probability negative hai, toh woh valid distribution hi nahi.
revision: Empirical P = favourable count / total observations.
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); P(not A) = 1 − P(A).
Valid distribution: har p ≥ 0 aur Σp = 1.
E[X] = Σ x · p(x) = long-run average.
Decision: har option ka expected profit nikalo, sabse zyada wala chuno.

questions.question: Ek e-commerce site pe kal 1,000 visitors aaye, jinme se 400 ne koi item cart me daala. Is data ke hisaab se ek naye visitor ke cart me item daalne ki empirical probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Empirical probability = 400 / 1000 = 0.4. Trap: 0.6 complement hai (cart me na daalne ki probability), 400 sirf count hai, aur 0.04 decimal galat jagah lagane se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek product ki weekly demand teen levels (Low, Medium, High) me se ek hoti hai. Inme se kaunsa set valid probability distribution hai?
questions.explanation: Valid distribution ke liye har probability 0 aur 1 ke beech ho aur sum exactly 1 ho. 0.25 + 0.35 + 0.40 = 1. Pehle set ka sum 1.1 hai, teesre (0.5 × 3) ka 1.5, aur doosre ka sum toh 1 hai par −0.1 negative hai, isliye invalid. Trap: sirf sum check karna aur negative value miss karna.

questions.question: Ek medical store me ek injection ki daily demand ka distribution: 5 units: 0.15, 6 units: 0.25, 7 units: 0.35, 8 units: 0.25. Store 6 units rakhta hai. Kisi din demand stock se zyada (yaani 7 ya usse zyada) hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(demand ≥ 7) = P(7) + P(8) = 0.35 + 0.25 = 0.6. Trap: sirf P(7) = 0.35 lena, ya P(demand ≥ 6) = 0.85 lena jisme 6 wala din bhi aa jaata hai, jab stock poora pad jaata hai.

questions.question: 200 customers ke survey me 120 UPI use karte hain, 90 card use karte hain, aur 50 dono use karte hain. Random customer UPI ya card (kam se kam ek) use kare, iski probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(UPI or card) = (120 + 90 − 50) / 200 = 160 / 200 = 0.8. Trap: overlap minus na karna, (120 + 90) / 200 = 1.05, jo 1 se zyada hai aur isliye impossible hai. 0.6 sirf UPI hai, 0.25 sirf 'dono' hai.

questions.question: Ek AC service company ko ek technician ke liye daily service calls ka distribution: 0 calls: 0.1, 1 call: 0.3, 2 calls: 0.4, 3 calls: 0.2. Expected number of calls per day kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = 0 × 0.1 + 1 × 0.3 + 2 × 0.4 + 3 × 0.2 = 0 + 0.3 + 0.8 + 0.6 = 1.7. Trap: values ka simple average (0 + 1 + 2 + 3) / 4 = 1.5 lena jo probabilities ignore karta hai, ya sabse likely value (mode = 2) ko expected value samajhna.

questions.question: Ek newspaper vendor har copy ₹4 me khareed ke ₹6 me bechta hai; bachi copies bekaar. Daily demand: 100 copies (prob 0.3), 150 copies (prob 0.5), 200 copies (prob 0.2). Agar woh 150 copies rakhe, toh uska expected daily profit kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cost = 150 × 4 = ₹600. Demand 100: revenue 100 × 6 = 600, profit 0. Demand 150 ya 200: sirf 150 bikti hain, revenue 900, profit 300. E[profit] = 0.3 × 0 + 0.7 × 300 = ₹210. Trap: maan lena ki saari 150 bik jaayengi (₹300), ya expected demand 145 pe profit 145 × 6 − 600 = ₹270 nikalna, jo uncertainty ko ignore karta hai.

weeks.title: Joint, marginal and conditional probability
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki contingency table se joint, marginal aur conditional probability kaise padhte hain, independence kaise check karte hain, aur total probability aur Bayes rule se quality aur marketing ke sawaal kaise solve karte hain.
concepts: **Contingency table** do categorical variables ke counts ek saath dikhati hai, jaise customers by region (Urban/Rural) aur plan (Premium/Basic). Har cell ko grand total se divide karo toh joint probability table ban jaati hai.
**Joint probability** P(A and B) ek cell / grand total hai. **Marginal probability** P(A) row ya column total / grand total hai; naam isliye kyunki yeh table ke 'margin' pe likhi hoti hai.
**Conditional probability** P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B): 'B pata hai, ab A ki probability'. Table me iska matlab hai cell ko B wali row ya column ke total se divide karna, grand total se nahi.
**Order matters**: P(Premium | Urban) aur P(Urban | Premium) alag cheezein hain. Pehla batata hai urban customers me premium ka share, doosra premium customers me urban ka share.

**Multiplication rule**: P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B | A). **Independence**: A aur B independent hain agar P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B), yaani P(A | B) = P(A). Table me iska matlab hai har row me proportions same hain.

**Law of total probability**: agar B1, B2 saare possibilities cover karte hain (jaise Plant A ya Plant B), toh P(D) = P(B1) P(D | B1) + P(B2) P(D | B2). Yeh 'overall defect rate' jaise sawaalon ke liye hai.

**Bayes rule** P(B1 | D) = P(B1) P(D | B1) / P(D) ulta sawaal answer karta hai: defective piece mila, toh woh Plant A se aaya hoga iski probability kya hai? Quality audits, fraud alerts aur lead scoring me yeh bahut use hota hai.

example.problem: Ek telecom company ke 400 customers: Urban me Premium 90, Basic 150; Rural me Premium 30, Basic 130. P(Urban and Premium), P(Premium), P(Premium | Urban), P(Urban | Premium) nikalo aur check karo ki region aur plan independent hain ya nahi.
steps: Totals: Urban = 90 + 150 = 240, Rural = 30 + 130 = 160, Premium = 90 + 30 = 120, Basic = 280, grand total = 400.
Conditional: P(Premium | Urban) = 90 / 240 = 0.375 (Urban row ke total se divide).
Ulta conditional: P(Urban | Premium) = 90 / 120 = 0.75 (Premium column ke total se divide).
Independence check: P(Premium | Urban) = 0.375 ≠ P(Premium) = 0.3. Equivalently 0.225 ≠ 0.6 × 0.3 = 0.18.
**Answer**: 0.225, 0.3, 0.375, 0.75; region aur plan **dependent** hain, urban customers premium zyada lete hain.

mistakes: Conditional probability me grand total se divide karna. 'Urban customers me premium ka share' ke liye Urban row ke total (240) se divide karo, 400 se nahi.
P(A | B) aur P(B | A) ko same samajhna. 75% premium customers urban hain, iska matlab yeh nahi ki 75% urban customers premium hain.
Bayes me sirf P(D | B) dekh ke answer dena. Base rate (har plant ka share) bhi lagta hai; pehle total P(D) nikalo, phir divide karo.
revision: Joint = cell / grand total; marginal = row ya column total / grand total.
P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B) = cell / B ka total.
Independent ⇔ P(A and B) = P(A) P(B) ⇔ P(A | B) = P(A).
Total probability: P(D) = Σ P(Bi) P(D | Bi).
Bayes: P(Bi | D) = P(Bi) P(D | Bi) / P(D).

questions.question: Ek supermarket ke 60% customers loyalty members hain. Members me se 40% sale day pe shopping karte hain. Random customer member ho AUR sale day pe shopping kare, iski probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Multiplication rule: P(member and sale day) = P(member) × P(sale day | member) = 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.24. Trap: sirf conditional 0.4 ko joint maan lena, ya 0.6 + 0.4 = 1.0 jodna; 'and' ke liye multiply hota hai.

questions.question: Do events A (customer ne ad dekha) aur B (customer ne product khareeda) independent kab kehlaayenge?
options: Jab P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)
Jab P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)
questions.explanation: Independence ki definition P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) hai; iska matlab ad dekhne se khareedne ki probability nahi badalti. Trap: P(A and B) = 0 mutually exclusive events ki condition hai (dono saath ho hi nahi sakte), independence ki nahi; aur P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) bhi exclusive events pe hi sach hota hai.

questions.question: 300 shoppers ka survey: Under 30 me Online 120, Offline 30; 30 ya usse zyada me Online 60, Offline 90. Ek random online shopper under 30 ho, iski probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Condition 'online' hai, toh Online column ka total lo: 120 + 60 = 180. P(Under 30 | Online) = 120 / 180 = 2/3 ≈ 0.67. Trap: 0.8 = 120 / 150 ulta conditional P(Online | Under 30) hai, 0.4 = 120 / 300 joint hai, aur 0.6 = 180 / 300 marginal P(Online) hai.

questions.question: Ek electronics chain ke 500 warranty claims: Brand X me Valid 120, Invalid 30; Brand Y me Valid 280, Invalid 70. Kya 'brand' aur 'claim valid hai ya nahi' independent hain?
options: Dependent, kyunki Brand Y ke claims zyada hain
Independent, kyunki dono brands me valid claims ka proportion 0.8 hai
Table se independence check nahi ho sakti
questions.explanation: P(Valid | X) = 120 / 150 = 0.8, P(Valid | Y) = 280 / 350 = 0.8, aur P(Valid) = 400 / 500 = 0.8. Conditional = marginal, toh independent. Trap: Brand Y ke zyada claims dekh ke dependent bolna; counts ka size nahi, row-wise proportions compare karte hain.

questions.question: Ek company ke phone chargers do plants se aate hain: Plant A 60% supply karta hai aur uske 2% defective hote hain; Plant B 40% supply karta hai aur uske 5% defective. Random charger defective ho, iski probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Total probability: P(D) = 0.6 × 0.02 + 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.012 + 0.020 = 0.032. Trap: 0.035 defect rates ka simple average hai jo supply share ignore karta hai, 0.07 = 0.02 + 0.05, aur 0.012 sirf Plant A ka hissa hai.

questions.question: Upar wale chargers me (Plant A: 60% supply, 2% defective; Plant B: 40% supply, 5% defective) ek customer ka charger defective nikla. Yeh Plant B se aaya ho, iski probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bayes: P(B | D) = P(B) P(D | B) / P(D) = (0.4 × 0.05) / 0.032 = 0.02 / 0.032 = 0.625. Plant B sirf 40% supply karta hai, par defective pieces ka 62.5% wahin se aata hai. Trap: 0.4 prior hai (defect ki info use hi nahi ki), 0.05 ulta conditional P(D | B) hai, aur 0.375 Plant A ka posterior hai.

weeks.title: Random variables, expected value and risk
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki discrete aur continuous random variables kya hote hain, expected value aur variance kaise nikaalte hain, aur insurance, pricing aur delivery jaise business problems me in se 'average outcome' aur 'risk' kaise naapte hain.
concepts: **Random variable (RV)** ek rule hai jo har uncertain outcome ko ek number deta hai, jaise 'kal kitne units bikenge' ya 'agla customer kitni der queue me rahega'. RV ki values pehle se pata nahi hoti, par unki probabilities model ki ja sakti hain.
**Discrete RV** countable values leta hai (orders ki ginti, defective items, calls). Iski **PMF** p(x) = P(X = x) har value ki probability batati hai, aur Σ p(x) = 1.

**Continuous RV** ek interval me koi bhi value le sakta hai (time, weight, distance). Iski **PDF** f(x) ke neeche ka area probability hai: P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = area from a to b. Kisi ek exact value ki probability 0 hoti hai, isliye P(X ≤ 5) = P(X < 5).

**Expected value** E[X] = Σ x · p(x) long-run average outcome hai. Business me isse **expected monetary value (EMV)** kehte hain: insurance premium, warranty cost ya average daily profit isi se plan hota hai.
**Variance aur SD risk naapte hain**: Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])², SD = √Var. Do options ka expected profit same ho sakta hai, par jiska SD kam hai woh kam risky hai.
**Linear functions**: Y = aX + b ho toh E[Y] = a E[X] + b aur Var(Y) = a² Var(X), SD(Y) = |a| SD(X). Fixed cost b expected value badalta hai par risk nahi.
**Continuous uniform** U(a, b): har value equally likely. P(X ≤ x) = (x − a) / (b − a), mean = (a + b) / 2, variance = (b − a)² / 12. Delivery window ya arrival time ka simple model.

example.problem: Ek insurance company ₹5,000 premium wali policy bechti hai. Saal me ₹2,00,000 ka claim aane ki probability 0.01, ₹50,000 ke claim ki 0.04, aur koi claim na aane ki 0.95 hai. Expected payout, company ka expected profit per policy, aur payout ka SD nikalo.
steps: Expected profit per policy = premium − E[X] = 5000 − 4000 = ₹1,000.
**Answer**: expected payout ₹4,000, expected profit ₹1,000 per policy, payout SD ₹22,000; ek policy bahut risky hai, isliye company hazaaron policies bech ke risk average karti hai.

mistakes: Variance me E[X²] − E[X] likh dena. Formula E[X²] − (E[X])² hai; mean ka square ghatao.
Var(aX + b) = a Var(X) + b likhna. Constant b variance pe asar nahi karta aur a square ho ke aata hai: a² Var(X).
Continuous RV me P(X = exact value) ko PDF ki value f(x) maan lena. f(x) density hai, probability nahi; exact value ki probability 0 hai.
revision: Discrete: PMF, Σ p = 1. Continuous: PDF, area = probability, P(X = a) = 0.
E[X] = Σ x p(x); Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])².
E[aX + b] = a E[X] + b; Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X).
U(a, b): P(X ≤ x) = (x − a)/(b − a), mean (a + b)/2.
Expected value = average outcome, SD = risk.

questions.question: Ek bank branch ke liye inme se kaunsa continuous random variable hai?
options: Ek ghante me aane wale customers ki ginti
Ek customer ka queue me wait time
Ek din me reject hue loan applications ki ginti
Ek din me khule naye accounts ki ginti
questions.explanation: Wait time kisi interval me koi bhi value le sakta hai (3.5 min, 3.57 min...), isliye continuous hai. Baaki teeno counts hain (0, 1, 2, ...), jo discrete hote hain. Trap: 'bade numbers' wale counts ko continuous samajhna; count hamesha discrete hai.

questions.question: Ek packet ka weight X (grams) ek continuous random variable hai jiski PDF f(x) hai. P(X = 500) kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Continuous RV me probability area se aati hai, aur ek single point ka area zero hota hai, isliye P(X = 500) = 0. Trap: f(500) ko probability samajhna; f(x) density hai aur 1 se bada bhi ho sakta hai.

questions.question: Ek furniture shop me roz bikne wale sofas X ka distribution: 0: 0.1, 1: 0.2, 2: 0.4, 3: 0.3. Har sofa pe ₹500 margin hai aur roz ka fixed cost ₹300 hai. Expected daily profit kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = 0 × 0.1 + 1 × 0.2 + 2 × 0.4 + 3 × 0.3 = 0.2 + 0.8 + 0.9 = 1.9. Profit = 500X − 300, toh E[profit] = 500 × 1.9 − 300 = ₹650. Trap: fixed cost bhool jaana (₹950), ya values ka simple average 1.5 use karna (500 × 1.5 − 300 = ₹450).

questions.question: Usi sofa distribution (0: 0.1, 1: 0.2, 2: 0.4, 3: 0.3) ke liye Var(X) kya hai?
Ek factory ka daily cost C = 200X + 1000 (₹) hai, jahan X roz ke breakdowns hain aur Var(X) = 4. Daily cost ka standard deviation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(C) = 200² × Var(X) = 40000 × 4 = 1,60,000, toh SD(C) = √160000 = ₹400. Equivalently SD(X) = 2 aur SD(C) = 200 × 2 = 400. Trap: ₹1,60,000 variance hai; ₹800 = 200 × 4 (variance ko SD samajh liya); ₹1,400 me fixed 1000 bhi jod diya jo spread nahi badalta.

questions.question: Ek quick-commerce app ka delivery time Uniform(20, 50) minutes maana gaya hai. Company aisa promise time t batana chahti hai ki 90% deliveries t minutes ke andar ho jaayein. t kya hoga?
questions.explanation: P(X ≤ t) = (t − 20) / (50 − 20) = 0.9 ⇒ t − 20 = 27 ⇒ t = 47 minutes. Trap: 0.9 × 50 = 45 lena (lower limit 20 bhool gaye), 27 sirf 0.9 × 30 hai (20 jodna bhool gaye), aur 35 mean hai jisse sirf 50% deliveries cover hoti hain.

weeks.title: Two random variables together: covariance and portfolios
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki do random variables ka joint distribution kaise padhte hain, covariance aur correlation se unka saath-saath chalna kaise naapte hain, aur sum, difference aur do-asset portfolio ka mean aur risk kaise nikaalte hain.
concepts: **Joint PMF** p(x, y) = P(X = x and Y = y) do RVs ki saath wali probabilities ki table hai, jaise X = cart me items, Y = coupon use hua ya nahi. Saari cells ka sum 1 hota hai.
**Marginal distribution**: kisi ek variable ki distribution, doosre pe sum karke. P(Y = 1) = Σ over x of p(x, 1), yaani table ka column total.
**Independence of RVs**: X aur Y independent hain agar har cell me p(x, y) = pX(x) · pY(y). Ek bhi cell me yeh fail ho jaaye toh dependent.

**Covariance** Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] − E[X] E[Y]. Positive matlab dono saath badhte hain (bade cart me coupon zyada), negative matlab ulta. Independent RVs ka covariance 0 hota hai (par 0 covariance hamesha independence nahi deta).
**Correlation** ρ = Cov(X, Y) / (σX σY), unit-free aur −1 se 1 ke beech. Covariance ki unit (₹ × units) confusing hoti hai, isliye strength compare karne ke liye ρ use karo.

**Sum aur difference ka variance**: Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2 Cov(X, Y) aur Var(X − Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) − 2 Cov(X, Y). Independent ho toh dono me Cov term 0. Dhyan do: difference me bhi variances judte hain.

**Portfolio**: weights w aur (1 − w) se R = w RA + (1 − w) RB. E[R] = w E[RA] + (1 − w) E[RB], aur Var(R) = w² σA² + (1 − w)² σB² + 2 w (1 − w) ρ σA σB. ρ jitna kam (ya negative), risk utna kam: yahi **diversification** hai.

**Business use**: do products ki demand ka correlation inventory pooling me, revenue aur cost ka covariance profit ke risk me, aur do business units ya assets ka correlation risk planning me use hota hai.

example.problem: Ek treasury team apne fund ka 60% asset A (expected return 12%, SD 20%) aur 40% asset B (expected return 8%, SD 10%) me rakhti hai. Dono ka correlation ρ = −0.5 hai. Portfolio ka expected return aur SD nikalo. (Yeh sirf ek textbook calculation hai, investment advice nahi.)
steps: w² σA² = 0.36 × 400 = 144 (SD % me hai, toh σA² = 20² = 400).
Compare: agar ρ = 0 hota toh Var = 160 aur SD ≈ 12.65%; negative correlation risk ghata raha hai.
**Answer**: expected return **10.4%**, SD ≈ **10.58%**; weighted average SD (16%) se kaafi kam.

mistakes: Var(X − Y) = Var(X) − Var(Y) likhna. Difference me bhi variances judte hain; sirf covariance ka sign badalta hai: Var(X) + Var(Y) − 2 Cov.
Portfolio SD ko assets ke SDs ka weighted average maan lena. Yeh sirf ρ = 1 pe sach hai; baaki cases me variance formula se nikalo.
Cov = 0 dekh ke independence declare karna. Independence ke liye har cell me p(x, y) = pX(x) pY(y) check karo.
revision: Marginal = joint table ka row ya column sum.
Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] − E[X] E[Y]; ρ = Cov / (σX σY).
Var(X ± Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) ± 2 Cov(X, Y).
Portfolio Var = w²σA² + (1 − w)²σB² + 2w(1 − w)ρσAσB.
ρ < 1 ⇒ diversification se risk kam hota hai.

questions.question: Ek online store me X = cart me items (1 ya 2) aur Y = coupon use hua (1) ya nahi (0). Joint PMF: p(1, 0) = 0.3, p(1, 1) = 0.1, p(2, 0) = 0.2, p(2, 1) = 0.4. P(Y = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Marginal: P(Y = 1) = p(1, 1) + p(2, 1) = 0.1 + 0.4 = 0.5. Trap: sirf ek cell lena (0.4 ya 0.1); marginal ke liye doosre variable ki saari values pe sum karna padta hai.

questions.question: Do alag shehron ke stores ki daily sales X aur Y independent hain, Var(X) = 9 aur Var(Y) = 16 (₹ hazaar² me). Combined sales X + Y ka variance kya hai?
questions.explanation: Independent ho toh Cov = 0, toh Var(X + Y) = 9 + 16 = 25. Trap: 5 = √25 SD hai, 7 = 3 + 4 SDs ka sum hai, aur 49 = (3 + 4)² jo SDs jodne se aata hai; SDs seedhe nahi judte, variances judte hain.

questions.question: Q1 wali joint PMF (p(1, 0) = 0.3, p(1, 1) = 0.1, p(2, 0) = 0.2, p(2, 1) = 0.4) ke liye Cov(X, Y) nikalo.
Usi joint PMF me kya X (cart size) aur Y (coupon use) independent hain?
options: Haan, kyunki saari probabilities ka sum 1 hai
Haan, kyunki covariance bahut chhota hai
Nahi, kyunki p(1, 1) sabse chhoti probability hai
questions.explanation: Independence ke liye har cell me p(x, y) = pX(x) pY(y) hona chahiye. p(2, 1) = 0.4 ≠ 0.3, toh dependent. Trap: sum = 1 sirf valid distribution batata hai, independence nahi; aur 'chhota covariance' bhi independence prove nahi karta (yahan Cov = 0.1 ≠ 0).

questions.question: Ek business unit ka monthly revenue R aur cost C hai (₹ lakh me): Var(R) = 100, Var(C) = 64, Cov(R, C) = 40. Profit P = R − C ka variance kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(R − C) = Var(R) + Var(C) − 2 Cov(R, C) = 100 + 64 − 80 = 84. Revenue aur cost saath badhte hain, isliye profit kam fluctuate karta hai. Trap: 36 = 100 − 64 (variances ghatana), 164 covariance ignore karna, aur 244 covariance ko plus karna.

questions.question: Ek fund ka 50% asset A (SD 10%) aur 50% asset B (SD 20%) me hai, aur dono ke returns ka correlation ρ = −0.4 hai. Portfolio return ka SD kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var = 0.25 × 100 + 0.25 × 400 + 2 × 0.5 × 0.5 × (−0.4) × 10 × 20 = 25 + 100 − 40 = 85, SD = √85 ≈ 9.22%. Trap: 15% SDs ka simple average hai (sirf ρ = 1 pe sahi), 11.18% = √125 correlation ignore karta hai, aur 12.85% = √165 covariance term ko plus le leta hai.

weeks.title: Binomial, Poisson and normal models in business
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki counts ke liye binomial aur Poisson model kab lagte hain, normal model aur z-score se probabilities kaise nikaalte hain, aur service level ya safety stock jaise decisions me inverse normal ka use kaise hota hai.
concepts: **Bernoulli trial** ka sirf do result hota hai: success (prob p) ya failure (1 − p), jaise ek visitor khareedega ya nahi. **Binomial** X = n independent trials me successes ki ginti, jab har trial me p same ho.
**Binomial formula**: P(X = k) = C(n, k) p^k (1 − p)^(n − k). Mean = np, variance = np(1 − p). Jaise 200 emails, open rate 5%: expected opens = 10.

**Poisson** ek fixed time ya space me random events ki ginti ka model hai (ek ghante me calls, ek page pe typos, mahine me crashes), jab events independent ho aur average rate λ constant ho. P(X = k) = e^(−λ) λ^k / k!, aur mean = variance = λ.
**Rate ko interval ke hisaab se scale karo**: 3 calls per 5 minute ho toh 10 minute ke liye λ = 6. Poisson binomial ka achha approximation bhi hai jab n bada aur p chhota ho, λ = np.

**Normal model** N(μ, σ) symmetric bell curve hai; packet weights, measurement errors, aur bahut saari cheezon ke sums ke liye achha fit. **z-score** z = (x − μ) / σ batata hai value mean se kitne SD door hai, phir standard normal table se probability.
**Empirical rule**: normal data ka lagbhag 68% μ ± σ me, 95% μ ± 2σ me aur 99.7% μ ± 3σ me hota hai. Quality control me ±3σ limits isi se aati hain.
**Inverse normal (service level)**: agar stock-out ki probability 5% rakhni hai toh stock = μ + z σ, jahan z = 1.645 (upper 5%). Common values: z(0.95) = 1.645, z(0.975) = 1.96, z(0.99) = 2.326.
**Model choose karna**: fixed n trials me success count → binomial; time/space me events ki ginti, koi upper limit nahi → Poisson; continuous measurement → normal.

example.problem: Ek bank ke call centre pe average 3 calls per 5 minutes aati hain (Poisson). Agle 5 minute me (a) koi call na aane ki, aur (b) zyada se zyada 2 calls aane ki probability nikalo.
steps: λ = 3 (5 minute ke interval ke liye).
**Answer**: (a) ≈ **0.0498**, (b) ≈ **0.4232**; yaani lagbhag 58% chance hai ki 5 minute me 3 ya zyada calls aayengi, staffing isi se plan karo.

mistakes: Poisson me λ ko interval ke hisaab se adjust na karna. Rate per hour diya ho aur sawaal 30 minute ka ho toh λ aadha karo.
z nikalte waqt SD ki jagah variance se divide karna. z = (x − μ) / σ, σ² nahi.
Binomial me C(n, k) bhool jaana. Exactly 1 success ke liye p(1 − p)^(n − 1) ko n se multiply karna padta hai, kyunki success kisi bhi trial me ho sakti hai.
revision: Binomial: P(X = k) = C(n, k) p^k (1 − p)^(n − k); mean np, var np(1 − p).
Poisson: P(X = k) = e^(−λ) λ^k / k!; mean = var = λ.
Stock for service level: μ + z σ (5% stock-out ⇒ z = 1.645).
Counts in n trials → binomial; events per interval → Poisson; measurements → normal.

questions.question: Ek bank counter pe ek ghante me aane wale customers ki ginti ke liye kaunsa model sabse natural hai?
questions.explanation: Yeh ek fixed time interval me random arrivals ki ginti hai, jiski koi fixed upper limit (n trials) nahi hai, isliye Poisson natural model hai. Trap: binomial ke liye fixed n trials aur har trial ka success/failure chahiye, jo yahan nahi hai.

questions.question: Ek marketing campaign me 200 emails bheje gaye aur har email ke khulne ki probability 0.05 hai (independently). Khule emails X ka mean aur variance kya hai?
questions.explanation: X ~ Binomial(200, 0.05). Mean = np = 200 × 0.05 = 10, variance = np(1 − p) = 10 × 0.95 = 9.5. Trap: Poisson ki tarah variance = mean = 10 maan lena; binomial me variance mean se thoda kam hota hai. 0.05 aur 0.0475 ek single email ke Bernoulli ke values hain.

questions.question: Ek car showroom me aane wale har visitor ke car khareedne ki probability 0.1 hai (independently). Aaj 5 visitors aaye. Exactly 1 ke khareedne ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 1) = C(5, 1) × 0.1 × 0.9⁴ = 5 × 0.1 × 0.6561 = 0.32805 ≈ 0.328. Trap: C(5, 1) = 5 bhool jaana, jisse 0.1 × 0.9⁴ ≈ 0.0656 aata hai (sirf ek specific visitor ka order); 0.5 = 5 × 0.1 expected value hai, probability nahi.

questions.question: Ek company ki website pe average 2 crashes per month hote hain (Poisson). Agle mahine ek bhi crash na hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 0) = e^(−2) × 2⁰ / 0! = e^(−2) ≈ 0.135. Trap: 0.865 = 1 − e^(−2) kam se kam ek crash ki probability hai; aur '0' isliye galat hai kyunki average 2 hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki har mahine crash hoga hi.

questions.question: Ek rice brand ke 1 kg packets ka actual weight N(μ = 1000 g, σ = 10 g) follow karta hai. Random packet 980 g se kam ho, iski probability kya hai? (Φ(2) = 0.9772 use karo.)
questions.explanation: z = (980 − 1000) / 10 = −2. P(Z < −2) = 1 − Φ(2) = 1 − 0.9772 = 0.0228. Trap: 0.0456 dono tails (< 980 ya > 1020) ka total hai, 0.4772 mean aur 980 ke beech ka area hai, aur 0.05 empirical rule ka 95% yaad karke galat tail lena hai.

questions.question: Ek warehouse me ek item ki daily demand N(μ = 500, σ = 80) units hai. Manager chahta hai ki kisi din stock-out ki probability sirf 5% ho. Kitne units stock rakhne chahiye? (z(0.95) = 1.645 use karo.)
questions.explanation: Stock S aisa ho ki P(demand > S) = 0.05, yaani S = μ + 1.645 σ = 500 + 1.645 × 80 = 500 + 131.6 = 631.6 ≈ 632 units. Trap: 1.96 use karna (657, jo do-tailed 95% ka z hai), z ko minus karna (368, jisse stock-out 95% ho jaata), ya sirf μ + σ = 580 lena (≈ 16% stock-out).

weeks.title: Central limit theorem and point estimation
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki sample mean ka apna distribution hota hai, central limit theorem kyun kehta hai ki woh lagbhag normal hai, aur unbiased estimator aur standard error ka matlab kya hai.
concepts: **Inference ka idea**: population ka parameter (μ, p, σ) pata nahi hota, isliye sample se statistic (x̄, p̂, s) nikaal ke uska andaaza lagaate hain. Har naya sample thoda alag x̄ dega; is variation ko samajhna hi inference ki neev hai.

**Sampling distribution of x̄**: agar same size n ke bahut saare samples lo aur har ek ka x̄ nikalo, toh un x̄ values ki distribution. Iska mean μ hota hai aur SD = σ / √n, jise **standard error (SE)** kehte hain.

**Central limit theorem (CLT)**: population ka shape kuch bhi ho (skewed income, skewed bill amount), agar n kaafi bada hai (rule of thumb n ≥ 30), toh x̄ lagbhag N(μ, σ / √n) hota hai. Isi wajah se business data skewed hone pe bhi mean ke liye normal table use kar paate hain.
**z for a sample mean**: z = (x̄ − μ) / (σ / √n). Galti se σ se divide kiya toh individual customer ka sawaal ban jaata hai, sample average ka nahi.
**Point estimator** ek formula hai jo sample se parameter ka ek number deta hai: x̄ for μ, p̂ = x / n for p, s² for σ².

**Unbiased estimator**: jiska expected value parameter ke barabar ho, E[θ̂] = θ. x̄ aur p̂ unbiased hain, aur s² = Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1) unbiased hai; n se divide karne wala version σ² ko average me thoda kam aankta hai.
**Efficiency aur SE**: do unbiased estimators me jiska variance (SE) kam ho woh better hai. SE = σ / √n, toh n ko 4 guna karne se SE aadha hota hai: precision ki keemat badi hoti hai.
**SE of a proportion**: SE(p̂) = √(p(1 − p) / n). Jaise 400 customers me 64% satisfied ho toh SE ≈ √(0.64 × 0.36 / 400) = 0.024, yaani ±2.4 percentage points ka typical error.

example.problem: Ek café chain me per-bill amount ka mean μ = ₹400 aur σ = ₹120 hai (distribution right-skewed). Ek din ke 36 random bills ka average ₹430 se zyada aane ki probability nikalo. (Φ(1.5) = 0.9332.)
steps: n = 36 ≥ 30, toh CLT se x̄ lagbhag normal hai, skewness ke bawajood.
Compare: ek single bill ke liye z = 30 / 120 = 0.25 hota, probability kaafi zyada. Averages individual values se kam fluctuate karte hain.

mistakes: Sample mean ke sawaal me σ / √n ki jagah σ use karna. Sawaal 'average of n' ka ho toh SE use karo.
Yeh sochna ki CLT population ko normal bana deta hai. CLT sirf x̄ ki distribution ke baare me hai; individual values ka shape waisa hi rehta hai.
Unbiased ka matlab 'har baar sahi' samajhna. Unbiased matlab average me sahi; ek sample ka estimate phir bhi galat ho sakta hai.
revision: E[x̄] = μ, SE(x̄) = σ / √n.
CLT: n ≥ 30 ⇒ x̄ ≈ N(μ, σ / √n), population ka shape kuch bhi ho.
Unbiased: E[θ̂] = θ; s² me (n − 1) se divide.

questions.question: Ek survey me 'saare Indian smartphone users ka average monthly data use' jaanna hai. Inme se kaunsa ek statistic hai (parameter nahi)?
questions.explanation: Statistic sample se nikla number hai, isliye 500 users ka x̄ statistic hai. μ, p aur σ poori population ke fixed (aur aam taur pe unknown) numbers hain, yaani parameters.

questions.question: Ek ATM se ek withdrawal ke amount ka σ = ₹50 hai. 100 random withdrawals ke sample mean ka standard error kya hai?
questions.explanation: SE = σ / √n = 50 / √100 = 50 / 10 = ₹5. Trap: ₹50 individual withdrawal ka SD hai, sample mean ka nahi; ₹0.5 = 50 / 100 (√ bhool gaye).

questions.question: Ek market research firm apne estimate ka standard error aadha karna chahti hai. Sample size ko kitna karna hoga?
questions.explanation: SE = σ / √n. SE ko aadha karne ke liye √n ko double karna padega, yaani n ko 4 guna. Trap: SE aur n ka relation linear maan ke 2 guna bolna; asal me SE √n se ghatta hai.

questions.question: Ek sample x₁, ..., xₙ se population variance σ² ka unbiased estimator kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1) ka expected value exactly σ² hai, isliye yeh unbiased hai. n se divide karne pe average me σ² se thoda kam aata hai (biased), kyunki x̄ khud sample se fit hua hai. Teesra option SD hai, variance nahi, aur range / 4 sirf rough estimate hai.

questions.question: Ek telecom company ne 400 customers ka survey kiya; 64% satisfied the. Is sample proportion ka standard error kya hai?
Ek credit card company ke customers ka monthly spend bahut right-skewed hai, μ = ₹2,000 aur σ = ₹600. 100 random customers ka average spend ₹1,880 se kam aane ki probability kya hai? (Φ(2) = 0.9772.)
options: Nikal nahi sakte, kyunki population skewed hai
questions.explanation: n = 100 bada hai, toh CLT se x̄ ≈ normal, SE = 600 / 10 = 60. z = (1880 − 2000) / 60 = −2, P = 1 − 0.9772 = 0.0228. Trap: σ se divide karna (z = −0.2, P ≈ 0.4207, jo ek single customer ka answer hai), ya skewness dekh ke haar maan lena; CLT isi situation ke liye hai. 0.9772 galat tail hai.

weeks.title: Sampling methods and sampling distributions
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki simple random, systematic, stratified aur cluster sampling kaise aur kab karte hain, bias kahan se aata hai, aur sample proportion aur finite population correction ke saath standard error kaise nikaalte hain.
concepts: **Sampling frame** woh list hai jisme se sample chunte ho (customer database, invoice register, store list). Frame me jo log hain hi nahi (jaise bina smartphone wale customers), woh kabhi sample me nahi aayenge: yeh **coverage bias** hai.
**Simple random sampling (SRS)**: frame ke har unit ka chune jaane ka chance barabar, aur har possible sample equally likely. Random number generator se 500 customer IDs chunna iska example hai.

**Systematic sampling**: k = N / n nikalo, 1 se k ke beech random start lo, phir har k-th unit lo. Jaise 5,000 invoices me se 100 chahiye toh k = 50; start 7 ho toh 7, 57, 107, ... Simple hai, par list me koi periodic pattern ho (har 7th din Sunday) toh bias aa sakta hai.

**Stratified sampling**: population ko homogeneous groups (strata) me baanto, jaise salaried / self-employed / retired, aur har stratum se alag random sample lo. **Proportional allocation**: stratum ka sample = n × (stratum size / N). Isse har important group represent hota hai aur SE aksar kam hota hai.

**Cluster sampling**: population pehle se naturally groups me hai (stores, villages, branches). Kuch clusters randomly chuno aur unke saare units survey karo. Travel aur cost bachta hai, par clusters ek doosre se alag ho toh precision kam hoti hai.

**Non-probability sampling** (convenience, judgement, voluntary online polls) sasta hai par **selection bias** deta hai: mall ke bahar survey karke poore shehar ki income ka andaaza galat hoga. Bada sample bias theek nahi karta.

**Sampling error vs non-sampling error**: sampling error random chance se aata hai aur n badhane se ghatta hai. Non-sampling error (galat questions, non-response, data entry galti) n badhane se nahi jaata.

**Sampling distribution of p̂**: mean p, SE = √(p(1 − p) / n), aur np ≥ 10, n(1 − p) ≥ 10 ho toh lagbhag normal. Jab sample population ka bada hissa ho (n / N > 5%), SE ko **finite population correction** √((N − n) / (N − 1)) se multiply karo.

example.problem: Ek bank ke 12,000 customers hain: 6,000 salaried, 4,000 self-employed, 2,000 retired. 300 customers ka survey karna hai. (a) Proportional stratified sample me har group se kitne? (b) Agar systematic sampling karein toh interval k kya hoga?
steps: (b) k = N / n = 12000 / 300 = 40; 1 se 40 ke beech random start lo, phir har 40th customer.

mistakes: Stratified aur cluster ko mix karna. Stratified me har group se kuch units lete ho; cluster me kuch groups poore ke poore lete ho aur baaki groups bilkul nahi.
Bade online poll ko reliable maan lena. Lakhon responses bhi selection bias theek nahi karte; sample random hona zaroori hai, sirf bada nahi.
Proportional allocation me har stratum ko barabar sample dena. Stratum ka sample uske population share ke proportion me hona chahiye.
revision: SRS: har unit ka equal chance; systematic: har k-th, k = N / n.
Stratified: har stratum se sample, proportional: n × Nh / N.
Cluster: kuch poore groups randomly chuno.
Bias n badhane se nahi jaata; random selection chahiye.

questions.question: Ek retail chain ke 80 stores hain. Woh randomly 10 stores chunti hai aur un 10 stores ke saare employees ka survey karti hai. Yeh kaunsa sampling method hai?
questions.explanation: Stores natural groups (clusters) hain; kuch clusters randomly chune aur unke andar sabko survey kiya, toh yeh cluster sampling hai. Trap: stratified samajhna; stratified me har store (group) se kuch employees lete, sirf kuch stores ke sab employees nahi.

questions.question: Ek auditor 5,000 invoices me se 100 ka systematic sample leta hai. Random start 7 aaya. Sample me teesra invoice kaunsa hoga?
questions.explanation: k = 5000 / 100 = 50. Sample: 7, 57, 107, ... toh teesra invoice 107 hai. Trap: 57 doosra invoice hai; 21 = 7 × 3 interval ki jagah start ko multiply karna hai; 150 = 3 × 50 start jodna bhool gaye.

questions.question: Ek company ke 2,000 employees hain: 1,200 plant me, 600 sales me, 200 office me. 150 employees ka proportional stratified sample lena hai. Sales se kitne employees chune jaayenge?
questions.explanation: Sales ka share = 600 / 2000 = 0.3, toh sample = 150 × 0.3 = 45. (Plant 90, office 15, total 150.) Trap: teen strata me barabar baantna (150 / 3 = 50), jo proportional allocation nahi hai; 60 = 600 / 10 galat fraction lena hai.

questions.question: Ek FMCG company apne Instagram page pe poll daal ke 'Indian households me green tea pine walon ka percentage' estimate karti hai; 50,000 responses aaye. Is estimate ki sabse badi problem kya hai?
options: Selection bias: poll me jawab dene wale poori households population ko represent nahi karte
Sampling error zero ho gaya hai, isliye estimate exact hai
Yeh stratified sample hai, isliye galat hai
questions.explanation: Sirf brand ke followers aur jo khud jawab dena chahte hain, woh sample me hain (voluntary, non-probability sample), toh estimate biased hoga. Trap: 50,000 ko bada dekh ke reliable maan lena; bada n sirf random error ghatata hai, bias nahi.

questions.question: Ek electronics store ke 30% customers EMI pe khareedte hain. 100 customers ka random sample liya jaayega. Sample proportion p̂ ki sampling distribution ka mean aur standard error kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[p̂] = p = 0.3 (unbiased). SE = √(0.3 × 0.7 / 100) = √0.0021 ≈ 0.046. Trap: 0.0021 variance hai (√ nahi liya), 0.21 = p(1 − p) hai jisme n hi nahi, aur mean 0.36 ka koi basis nahi; p̂ ka centre hamesha p pe hota hai.

questions.question: Ek district me 500 kirana shops hain aur unki monthly sales ka σ = ₹20,000 hai. Bina replacement 100 shops ka random sample liya. Finite population correction ke saath x̄ ka standard error kya hai?

weeks.title: Confidence intervals and sample size
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki mean aur proportion ke liye confidence interval kaise banate hain (z aur t dono), uska sahi matlab kya hai, margin of error kis cheez pe depend karta hai, required sample size kaise nikaalte hain, aur do means ke difference ka interval kaise banta hai.
concepts: **Interval estimate** = point estimate ± margin of error. Ek number (x̄ = ₹430) ki jagah range (₹410 se ₹450) dena zyada honest hai, kyunki sample se exact μ kabhi pata nahi chalta.
**σ known (z-interval)**: x̄ ± z × σ / √n. 90%, 95%, 99% ke liye z = 1.645, 1.96, 2.576. Margin of error (ME) = z × SE.
**σ unknown (t-interval)**: x̄ ± t × s / √n, jahan t ki degrees of freedom n − 1 hain. t ki tails z se moti hoti hain, isliye chhote samples me interval wider aata hai; n bada ho toh t ≈ z.

**Sahi interpretation**: '95% confidence' ka matlab hai ki agar yeh process baar baar dohraayein toh lagbhag 95% intervals asli μ ko cover karenge. Ek banne ke baad interval ya toh μ ko contain karta hai ya nahi; aur yeh individual customers ke 95% ki range nahi hai.
**ME kis pe depend karta hai**: confidence level badhao toh ME badhta hai, σ zyada toh ME zyada, n zyada toh ME kam (√n ke hisaab se). Precision aur confidence ke beech trade-off hai.
**Sample size for a mean**: n = (z σ / E)², hamesha upar round karo. **For a proportion**: n = z² p(1 − p) / E²; p ka andaaza na ho toh p = 0.5 lo, jo sabse bada (safe) n deta hai.
**Proportion ka CI**: p̂ ± z √(p̂(1 − p̂) / n), jab np̂ aur n(1 − p̂) dono kam se kam 10 ho.
**Do means ka difference** (independent samples, σ known ya n bade): (x̄₁ − x̄₂) ± z √(σ₁² / n₁ + σ₂² / n₂). Agar interval me 0 nahi hai toh data dono groups me asli farq ki taraf ishaara karta hai.

example.problem: Ek logistics company ke 25 random delivery agents roz average x̄ = 82 km chalate hain, sample SD s = 10 km. μ ke liye 95% confidence interval banao. (t(0.025, 24) = 2.064 use karo.)
steps: σ unknown hai aur n = 25 chhota hai, toh t-interval lagega, df = 25 − 1 = 24.
z = 1.96 lagate toh ME = 3.92 hota; t thoda wider interval deta hai kyunki s bhi estimate hai.

mistakes: CI ko individual values ki range samajhna. (₹410, ₹450) average bill ka interval hai; bahut saare customers ke bill isse bahut bahar honge.
Sample size ko neeche round karna. n = 245.86 aaye toh 246 lo; 245 lene se required margin poora nahi hoga.
Do means ke difference ke SE me SEs ko jodna. Variances jodo phir √ lo: √(σ₁²/n₁ + σ₂²/n₂), na ki σ₁/√n₁ + σ₂/√n₂.
revision: z-CI: x̄ ± z σ/√n; t-CI: x̄ ± t s/√n, df = n − 1.
Confidence ↑ ⇒ ME ↑; n ↑ ⇒ ME ↓.
n = (zσ/E)², proportion ke liye z²p(1 − p)/E²; hamesha upar round.
Difference CI: (x̄₁ − x̄₂) ± z √(σ₁²/n₁ + σ₂²/n₂); 0 bahar ⇒ farq.

questions.question: Ek restaurant chain ne average bill ke liye 95% confidence interval (₹410, ₹450) nikala. Iska sabse sahi matlab kya hai?
options: 95% customers ka bill ₹410 aur ₹450 ke beech hai
Is particular interval me μ hone ki probability 0.95 hai, aur yeh baat har baar exact sach hai
Yahi method baar baar use karein toh lagbhag 95% intervals asli average bill μ ko cover karenge
Sample mean 95% baar ₹410 aur ₹450 ke beech aayega
questions.explanation: Confidence level method ke baare me hai: lambe run me 95% aise intervals μ ko pakadte hain. Trap: isse individual customers ki range samajhna (option A), jabki yeh average ka interval hai; aur ek bana hua interval ya toh μ ko contain karta hai ya nahi.

questions.question: Same sample (same n, same x̄, same σ) se confidence level 95% se badha ke 99% kar diya. Interval pe kya asar hoga?
questions.explanation: Zyada confidence ke liye bada z chahiye (2.576 vs 1.96), toh ME badhta hai aur interval wider hota hai. Centre x̄ hi rehta hai. Trap: sochna ki zyada confidence matlab zyada precise (narrower) answer; asal me confidence aur precision ka trade-off hai.

questions.question: Ek fintech app ke 64 random users ka average monthly UPI spend x̄ = ₹1,200 hai, aur σ = ₹240 known hai. μ ke liye 95% confidence interval kya hai? (z = 1.96)

Ek insurance company average claim amount ₹50 ke margin of error ke andar, 95% confidence ke saath estimate karna chahti hai. Pichhle data se σ ≈ ₹400. Kam se kam kitne claims ka sample chahiye? (z = 1.96)
questions.explanation: n = (z σ / E)² = (1.96 × 400 / 50)² = 15.68² = 245.86, upar round karke 246. Trap: square karna bhool jaana (15.68 ≈ 16), z bhool jaana ((400 / 50)² = 64), ya 90% wala z = 1.645 lagana ((1.645 × 8)² ≈ 173.2 → 174).

questions.question: Ek survey me 400 mobile users me se 120 ne kaha ki woh agle saal network badal sakte hain. Is proportion ke liye 95% confidence interval kya hai? (z = 1.96)
Mall stores: n₁ = 50, x̄₁ = ₹820, σ₁ = ₹150. High-street stores: n₂ = 40, x̄₂ = ₹760, σ₂ = ₹120. μ₁ − μ₂ ke liye 95% CI aur uska conclusion kya hai? (z = 1.96)
options: (₹4.2, ₹115.8): 0 interval me nahi hai, toh mall stores ka average bill zyada lagta hai
(−₹18.8, ₹138.8): 0 interval me hai, toh farq ka saboot nahi
(₹31.5, ₹88.5): mall stores ka average bill zyada lagta hai
(₹4.2, ₹115.8): interval positive hai par dono me koi farq nahi
questions.explanation: SE = √(150² / 50 + 120² / 40) = √(450 + 360) = √810 ≈ 28.46. ME = 1.96 × 28.46 ≈ 55.8. CI = 60 ± 55.8 = (4.2, 115.8). Poora interval 0 se upar hai, toh mall stores ka μ zyada lagta hai. Trap: SEs ko seedha jodna (21.21 + 18.97 = 40.19, jisse (−18.8, 138.8) aata hai), sirf ±1 SE lena (31.5 se 88.5), ya sahi interval ka galat conclusion.

weeks.title: Testing business claims with hypothesis tests
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki kisi business claim ko null aur alternative hypothesis me kaise likhte hain, proportion ke liye z-test aur mean ke liye t-test kaise karte hain, p-value ka matlab kya hai, aur Type I, Type II error aur power kya hote hain.
concepts: **Null hypothesis H₀** 'status quo' ya claim ka default version hai (koi farq nahi, μ = 500). **Alternative H₁** woh hai jiska saboot dhoondh rahe ho (μ > 500, p < 0.90, μ ≠ 6). Hypotheses hamesha parameters (μ, p) ke baare me hoti hain, x̄ ya p̂ ke baare me nahi.

**One-tailed vs two-tailed**: 'badha hai', 'kam hai' jaise directional claim → one-tailed (H₁: μ > μ₀ ya μ < μ₀). 'Badla hai' ya 'alag hai' → two-tailed (H₁: μ ≠ μ₀), jisme α dono tails me bant jaata hai.

**Test statistic** batata hai sample result H₀ se kitne SE door hai. Proportion: z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1 − p₀) / n), dhyan do SE me p₀ lagta hai, p̂ nahi. Mean (σ unknown): t = (x̄ − μ₀) / (s / √n), df = n − 1.

**p-value**: agar H₀ sach ho toh itna ya isse zyada extreme result aane ki probability. Chhota p-value matlab data H₀ ke saath fit nahi baithta. **Decision rule**: p-value < α (jaise 0.05) ⇒ reject H₀; warna 'fail to reject' (H₀ prove nahi hota, bas saboot kaafi nahi).
**Critical value approach**: test statistic ko critical value se compare karo. Two-tailed 5% z-test me |z| > 1.96 ho toh reject; t-test me t table ki value use karo (jaise t(0.025, 24) = 2.064).

**Type I error** (α): H₀ sach hai phir bhi reject kar diya, jaise achhe batch ko galti se reject karna. **Type II error** (β): H₀ galat hai phir bhi reject nahi kiya, jaise kharab batch pass kar dena. α ghatane se (baaki sab same) β badhta hai.
**Power** = 1 − β = H₀ galat hone pe use sahi se reject karne ki probability. Power badhti hai jab n bada ho, asli effect bada ho, σ chhota ho, ya α bada ho.
**Statistical vs practical significance**: bahut bade sample me ₹2 ka farq bhi 'significant' aa sakta hai, par business ke liye bekaar ho sakta hai. Decision me effect ka size bhi dekho.

example.problem: Ek courier company claim karti hai ki 90% parcels time pe pahunchte hain. Ek e-commerce client ne 400 random parcels check kiye; 344 time pe the. 5% level pe test karo ki kya on-time rate 90% se kam hai. (Φ(−2.67) ≈ 0.0038)
steps: H₀: p = 0.90, H₁: p < 0.90 (left-tailed, kyunki client ko 'kam' hone ka shak hai).
0.0038 < 0.05, toh H₀ reject. (Critical value se bhi: −2.67 < −1.645.)
**Answer**: z ≈ −2.67, p-value ≈ 0.0038; **reject H₀**, data ke hisaab se on-time rate 90% se kam lagta hai.

mistakes: Fail to reject ko 'H₀ prove ho gaya' bolna. Saboot kaafi nahi hai, bas itna; H₀ sach hai yeh nahi kehte.
p-value ko 'H₀ sach hone ki probability' samajhna. p-value H₀ maan ke data ki probability hai, H₀ ki probability nahi.
Proportion test ke SE me p̂ daalna. Test H₀ ke under hota hai, isliye SE = √(p₀(1 − p₀) / n).
revision: H₀: status quo (=, ≤, ≥); H₁: jiska saboot chahiye (≠, >, <).
z = (p̂ − p₀)/√(p₀q₀/n); t = (x̄ − μ₀)/(s/√n), df = n − 1.
p-value < α ⇒ reject H₀.
Type I = sach H₀ reject (α); Type II = galat H₀ accept (β).
Power = 1 − β; n bada ⇒ power zyada.

questions.question: Ek quality team ka H₀: 'batch theek hai (defect rate 2%)'. Type I error kya hoga?
options: Batch sach me theek tha, phir bhi reject kar diya
Batch kharab tha, phir bhi pass kar diya
Batch kharab tha aur reject kar diya
Sample size bahut chhota rakh diya
questions.explanation: Type I error = H₀ sach hai par reject kar diya; yahan achha batch galti se reject hona. Trap: option B Type II error hai (galat H₀ ko reject na karna), aur option C to sahi decision hai.

questions.question: Ek A/B test me naye checkout page ke liye p-value = 0.03 aaya, aur significance level α = 0.05 hai. Sahi decision kya hai?
options: H₀ accept karo, kyunki 0.03 bahut chhota hai
H₀ ke galat hone ki probability 97% hai
Is information se koi decision nahi ho sakta
H₀ reject karo, kyunki p-value α se kam hai
questions.explanation: Rule: p-value < α ⇒ reject H₀. 0.03 < 0.05, toh reject. Trap: '97% probability H₀ galat hai' bolna; p-value H₀ maan ke data ki probability hai, H₀ ki probability nahi.

questions.question: Ek sales manager claim karta hai ki nayi packaging se ek store ki average daily sales 500 units se zyada ho gayi hai. Uska claim test karne ke liye sahi hypotheses kya hain?
questions.explanation: Jis claim ka saboot chahiye ('500 se zyada') woh H₁ me jaata hai, aur H₀ status quo hai: μ ≤ 500 (ya μ = 500). Trap: claim ko H₀ me rakhna (option A); two-tailed ≠ lena jabki claim directional hai; aur hypothesis x̄ pe likhna, jabki hypotheses parameter μ ke baare me hoti hain.

questions.question: Ek brand claim karta hai ki 40% customers uska product prefer karte hain. 200 customers ke sample me 70 ne prefer kiya. H₀: p = 0.40 ke liye z-statistic kya hai?

Ek support centre claim karta hai ki average call handling time 6 minute hai. 25 random calls ka x̄ = 6.6 minute aur s = 1.5 minute aaya. 5% level pe two-tailed t-test ka result kya hai? (t(0.025, 24) = 2.064)
options: t = 2.0, fail to reject H₀, kyunki |t| < 2.064
questions.explanation: t = (6.6 − 6) / (1.5 / √25) = 0.6 / 0.3 = 2.0. Two-tailed critical value 2.064 hai, aur |2.0| < 2.064, toh fail to reject H₀. Trap: 2.0 ko z ka 1.96 se compare karke reject karna (chhote sample me t table chahiye), s / √n ki jagah s use karna (t = 0.4), ya √n ki jagah n se divide karna (t = 10).

questions.question: Ek retail chain test karti hai H₀: μ = 100 vs H₁: μ > 100 (average weekly sales per store, ₹ hazaar me), σ = 15, n = 36, α = 0.05 (z = 1.645). Agar asli μ = 105 ho, toh test ki power kya hai? (Φ(0.355) ≈ 0.639)
questions.explanation: SE = 15 / 6 = 2.5. Reject agar x̄ > 100 + 1.645 × 2.5 = 104.11. μ = 105 pe: P(x̄ > 104.11) = P(Z > (104.11 − 105) / 2.5) = P(Z > −0.355) ≈ 0.639 ≈ 0.64. Trap: 0.36 β (Type II error) hai, 0.05 α hai, aur 0.95 = 1 − α hai jiska power se seedha rishta nahi.

weeks.title: Simple linear regression for business data
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki do variables (jaise ad spend aur sales) ke beech least-squares line kaise fit karte hain, slope aur intercept ka business matlab kya hai, residuals aur R² se fit kaise judge karte hain, aur ANOVA table aur model ki conditions kya hain.
concepts: **Model**: y = β₀ + β₁x + ε, jahan y response hai (sales), x predictor hai (ad spend), aur ε random error hai. Sample se estimated line ŷ = b₀ + b₁x hoti hai.

**Least squares**: woh line jo residuals ke squares ka sum Σ(y − ŷ)² minimum kare. Formula: b₁ = Sxy / Sxx, jahan Sxy = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) aur Sxx = Σ(x − x̄)², aur b₀ = ȳ − b₁ x̄. Line hamesha (x̄, ȳ) se guzarti hai.

**Interpretation**: slope b₁ = x me 1 unit badhne pe predicted y me average change (₹1 lakh zyada ad spend ⇒ ₹b₁ lakh zyada predicted sales). Intercept b₀ = x = 0 pe predicted y, jo tabhi meaningful hai jab x = 0 data ki range ke paas ho.
**Residual** e = y − ŷ = actual − predicted. Positive residual matlab model ne kam predict kiya. Least-squares line ke residuals ka sum 0 hota hai.

**Variation ka breakdown**: SST = Σ(y − ȳ)² (total), SSR = Σ(ŷ − ȳ)² (model se explained), SSE = Σ(y − ŷ)² (unexplained), aur SST = SSR + SSE. **R² = SSR / SST** = y ke variation ka kitna hissa x explain karta hai; simple regression me R² = r².

**ANOVA table**: Regression: df = 1, MSR = SSR / 1. Error: df = n − 2, MSE = SSE / (n − 2). F = MSR / MSE; bada F matlab slope zero nahi lagta. **Standard error of estimate** s = √MSE, predictions ka typical error.

**Conditions (LINE)**: Linear relation, Independent errors, Normal errors, Equal variance. Residual plot me curve dikhe toh linearity tooti; funnel (x ke saath spread badhta) dikhe toh equal variance tooti; time order me pattern dikhe toh independence tooti.
**Cautions**: data ki range ke bahar prediction (extrapolation) risky hai, ek outlier slope ko bahut khisak sakta hai, aur strong regression bhi causation prove nahi karta.

example.problem: 5 mahino ka data, ad spend x (₹ lakh): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 aur sales y (₹ lakh): 12, 15, 19, 20, 24. Regression line, x = 6 pe prediction, aur R² nikalo.
steps: x = 6: ŷ = 9.3 + 17.4 = 26.7 (dhyan do: 6 data range ke bahar hai, thoda extrapolation hai).
**Answer**: ŷ = **9.3 + 2.9x**, x = 6 pe ŷ = **₹26.7 lakh**, R² ≈ **0.978** (sales ke variation ka lagbhag 98% ad spend se explain).

mistakes: Slope ka matlab ulta padhna. ŷ = 50 + 4.5x me x (ad spend) 1 badhe toh predicted y 4.5 badhta hai, ulta nahi; regression y on x aur x on y alag lines hain.
Residual ko predicted − actual likhna. Residual = actual − predicted (y − ŷ); sign galat hua toh interpretation ulti ho jaati hai.
MSE me n − 2 ki jagah n − 1 ya n se divide karna. Simple regression me do parameters (b₀, b₁) estimate hote hain, isliye error df = n − 2.
revision: b₁ = Sxy / Sxx, b₀ = ȳ − b₁x̄.
Residual = y − ŷ; Σ residuals = 0.
SST = SSR + SSE; R² = SSR / SST = r².
ANOVA: F = (SSR / 1) / (SSE / (n − 2)).
LINE conditions; funnel residual plot ⇒ unequal variance.

questions.question: Ek company ka fitted model hai: Sales = 50 + 4.5 × AdSpend (dono ₹ lakh me). Slope 4.5 ka sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Ad spend zero ho toh sales ₹4.5 lakh hogi
Sales ₹1 lakh badhe toh ad spend ₹4.5 lakh badhega
Ad spend aur sales ka correlation 4.5 hai
Ad spend ₹1 lakh badhne pe predicted sales average ₹4.5 lakh badhti hai
questions.explanation: Slope = x me 1 unit change pe predicted y ka change. Trap: option A intercept wala matlab hai (aur intercept 50 hai, 4.5 nahi), option B direction ulta kar deta hai, aur correlation kabhi 1 se bada nahi hota.

questions.question: Store size (sq ft) se monthly sales predict karne wale model ka R² = 0.81 hai. Iska matlab kya hai?
options: Monthly sales ke variation ka 81% store size se explain hota hai
questions.explanation: R² = SSR / SST = y ke variation ka explained hissa. Trap: R² ko r samajhna; r = ±√0.81 = ±0.9 hoga, 0.81 nahi. R² ka predictions ke 'exactly sahi' hone se ya slope se koi seedha rishta nahi.

questions.question: Ek dataset me x̄ = 5, ȳ = 30, Sxy = 120 aur Sxx = 40 hai. Least-squares line se x = 8 pe predicted y kya hai?
questions.explanation: b₁ = 120 / 40 = 3, b₀ = 30 − 3 × 5 = 15. ŷ = 15 + 3 × 8 = 39. Trap: intercept bhool ke sirf 3 × 8 = 24 lena, ya ȳ ko intercept maan ke 30 + 24 = 54 lena; 33 = 30 + 3 sirf ek step badhana hai.

questions.question: Fitted line ŷ = 9.3 + 2.9x hai (x = ad spend, y = sales, dono ₹ lakh). Ek mahine x = 4 tha aur actual sales y = 20 thi. Is mahine ka residual kya hai?
questions.explanation: ŷ = 9.3 + 2.9 × 4 = 9.3 + 11.6 = 20.9. Residual = y − ŷ = 20 − 20.9 = −0.9 (model ne thoda zyada predict kiya). Trap: ŷ − y lena (+0.9), predicted value 20.9 ko hi residual likhna, ya sirf slope wala hissa 11.6.

questions.question: 20 stores pe simple regression ka ANOVA: SST = 500, SSE = 140. F-statistic kya hai?
Price (x) aur units sold (y) ke data me Sxx = 200, Syy = 450 aur Sxy = −240 hai. y on x regression ka slope b₁ aur correlation r kya hain?
questions.explanation: b₁ = Sxy / Sxx = −240 / 200 = −1.2. r = Sxy / √(Sxx × Syy) = −240 / √90000 = −240 / 300 = −0.8. Price badhe toh units ghatte hain, toh dono negative. Trap: Syy se divide karna (−0.53, jo x on y ka slope hai), r ki jagah R² = 0.64 likhna, ya sign chhod dena.
